method.selection: One pair per content workload, fixed before collecting new scores. Both platforms use the same route.
method.google: Three fresh analyses per URL; collect mobile and desktop; compare per-page medians.
method.debugbear: Planned one fresh run per URL and device in US East, mobile and desktop kept separate. Repeated service errors stopped collection after 20 completed reports: five matched mobile pairs and four matched desktop pairs, plus two unpaired reports.
method.pingdom: One fresh run per URL from the same city for every pair.
method.gtmetrix: One fresh run per URL if account quota permits.
method.webpagetest: One fresh run per URL with matched settings if quota permits.
method.order: Alternate platform order between pairs and Google rounds. Never retry just for a better score.

contentChecks.details: Both hosts show the OK response, all eight expanded option fields, and the same three code examples. Docs7 adds a required label on the response; Mintlify adds related-topic links.
Both hosts render YouTube video 5As9tZMN3a8, the same feature and quickstart catalog, and the same workflow illustration. Mintlify inserts the video iframe after initial hydration.
Both hosts render the same ready badge from the custom Status component. Mintlify inserts the badge after hydration.
Both hosts render the Write → Preview → Publish SVG diagram.
Rendered equations differ. Mintlify displays raw math text.

contentFindings.reason: Content mismatch: Docs7 renders E=mc² and a stacked fraction; Mintlify displays raw E = mc^2 and \frac12. Confirmed after hydration with rendered DOM and screenshot. Excluded from comparisons.

notes: Third-party hosted tests only. No local Lighthouse or HTTP measurements are included.
Google uses three completed runs per URL and device; comparisons use medians. Timing values were transcribed from Google's score-calculator links; CLS there is rounded to two decimals.

DebugBear uses one run per URL and device with its own settings; its Lighthouse scores are not pooled with Google's. Repeated service errors limited coverage to five matched mobile pairs and four matched desktop pairs. Unpaired reports remain in results only.
Pingdom pairs use San Francisco. An initial Mintlify overview run used London and remains in results with comparisonEligible=false.
These are initial page loads of deployed sites with their integrations, not a controlled comparison of rendering engines. CDN cache state was not controlled.
GTmetrix and WebPageTest reached their free test limits. Their complete pairs are shown separately and are not included in the overview charts.
